criteria.text: Diagnosis of congenital or acquired generalized lipodystrophy (approval criterion 3).
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with an endocrinologist or cardiologist (approval criterion 2).
At least one additional diagnosis: diabetes mellitus, triglycerides ≥200 mg/dL, or fasting insulin ≥30 μU/mL (approval criterion 4).
Baseline HbA1C, triglycerides, and fasting insulin have all been obtained prior to beginning therapy (approval criterion 5).
Myalept is used as an adjunct to diet modification (approval criterion 6).
Physician is enrolled in the Myalept REMS Program (approval criterion 7).
Patient does not have HIV-related lipodystrophy (denial criterion 2).
Patient does not have partial lipodystrophy (denial criterion 3).
Patient does not have liver disease, including non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) (denial criterion 4).
Patient does not have general obesity unassociated with congenital leptin deficiency (denial criterion 5).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Myalept (metreleptin), a leptin analog used as an adjunct to diet as replacement therapy for complications of leptin deficiency in congenital or acquired generalized lipodystrophy. Version 1; Original 10/11/2021; Approval 11/19/2021; Effective 1/4/2022.

Encoded: approval criteria 1–7 and denial exclusions for HIV-related lipodystrophy, partial lipodystrophy, liver disease including NASH, and general obesity not associated with congenital leptin deficiency. Failure to meet approval criteria is also a denial. REMS enrollment applies to the physician.
Cautions (notes only): monitor for anti-metreleptin antibodies with neutralizing activity.
Cautions (notes only): insulin or insulin secretagogue dose adjustment, including possible large reductions, may be necessary. Closely monitor blood glucose during concomitant therapy.
Cautions (notes only): autoimmune disorder progression has been observed; carefully consider treatment benefits and risks in patients with autoimmune disease.

Cautions (notes only): carefully consider treatment benefits and risks in patients with significant hematologic abnormalities and/or acquired generalized lipodystrophy. Acquired generalized lipodystrophy remains an allowed indication.

Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 6 months if the prescriber documents a positive clinical response and continued use as an adjunct to dietary modifications.
Quantity (notes only): maximum dose 10 mg/day (up to 1 vial per day). max_units is null; dosing and quantity are not evaluated.
Documentation verification, cautions, ongoing monitoring, duration, reauthorization response, dosing, and quantity limits require manual review; this pack remains partial.
